IGF-I-induced signaling and growth of MCF- 7 breast cancer cells are mediated by ERalpha.
IGF-I-induced signaling and growth responses in ERalpha-containing breast cancer cells require the presence of functional ERalpha.

IGF-I-induced signaling events, including Akt and extracellular signal-regulated kinase activation, induction of cyclin expression and enhanced cell proliferation are dependent on ERalpha in MCF- 7 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IGF-I-induced proliferation and G(1)-to-S-phase transition in MCF- 7 cells are dependent on ERalpha.
IGF-I induces proliferation of MFC-7 cells through activation of the PI3-K/Akt signaling pathway, and this response is mediated by ERalpha.
IGF-I-induced mitogenic responses are mediated through ERalpha in MCF- 7 breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ERalpha is required for IGF-I-induced mitogenic responses in MCF cells.
IGF-I-induced proliferation of MCF7 cells is dependent on PI3-K and ERalpha and that ERalpha is required for IGF-I-induced Akt and MAPK activation and induction of cyclin E and cyclin D1.
